type-test: A type test is one of the type tests of clause 6 ([[iec-56]] 6 / IEC 694 clause 6), made on a representative circuit-breaker to verify that the design meets its rated characteristics — as distinct from a routine test made on every unit. For IEC 56, the type tests comprise [[dielectric-test]]s (6.1), [[radio-interference-voltage-test]]s (6.2), [[temperature-rise-test]]s (6.3), main-circuit resistance (6.4), short-time/peak withstand current tests (6.5), [[mechanical-and-environmental-test]]s (6.101), and short-circuit making and breaking tests including terminal-fault, short-line-fault and out-of-phase tests (6.102-6.110), plus capacitive and small-inductive switching. In principle each is performed on a new, clean circuit-breaker; tests may be done at different times and locations, and the manufacturer's responsibility is limited to the specified values ([[iec-56]] 6 intro). See [[short-circuit-test]] and [[test-duty]].
dielectric-test: The dielectric test verifies that the circuit-breaker withstands the overvoltages defined by its [[rated-insulation-level]], proving the integrity of insulation to earth, between poles and across the open gap. Per [[iec-56]] 6.1 (with IEC 694 6.1), it comprises power-frequency withstand tests (6.1.7), lightning-impulse and switching-impulse voltage tests (6.1.6) at the rated withstand voltages, plus wet tests for outdoor breakers and artificial-pollution tests (6.1.8). Test voltages and conditions follow Tables IV/VIII-X. For breakers at or above 300 kV the open-gap power-frequency test applies 2.5 U/sqrt(3) across the break using two out-of-phase sources; impulse tests across the open break may add 0.7 U sqrt(2)/sqrt(3) to U_p. Self-restoring external insulation passing on repeat after a single disruptive wet-test discharge is acceptable ([[iec-56]] 6.1.7). Related: [[partial-discharge-test]], [[radio-interference-voltage-test]].
radio-interference-voltage-test: The radio-interference-voltage (RIV) test checks that corona and surface discharges from the high-voltage parts do not generate excessive radio-frequency noise. Per [[iec-56]] 6.2 (and IEC 694 6.2), RIV tests are performed only by agreement between manufacturer and user. The standard adds that tests may be carried out on one pole of the circuit-breaker, in both the closed and the open positions, the RIV being measured at a specified test voltage against the limit set in the base standard ([[iec-56]] 6.2). It is one of the dielectric-family [[type-test]]s and complements the [[dielectric-test]] and the [[partial-discharge-test]] in characterising the insulation and external corona behaviour of the apparatus.
partial-discharge-test: The partial-discharge test detects internal discharges in insulation that would otherwise degrade it over time. Per [[iec-56]] 6.1.9 (with IEC 694 6.1.9), no partial-discharge test is required on the complete circuit-breaker. However, where the breaker uses components for which a relevant IEC publication prescribes partial-discharge measurement — for example bushings to IEC 137 (Bushings for Alternating Voltages above 1000 V) — the manufacturer must produce evidence that those components have passed the partial-discharge tests laid down in the applicable component standard ([[iec-56]] 6.1.9). It is grouped under the dielectric [[type-test]]s alongside the [[dielectric-test]] and [[radio-interference-voltage-test]], supporting the [[rated-insulation-level]].
temperature-rise-test: The temperature-rise test verifies that, carrying its [[rated-normal-current]] continuously, the circuit-breaker's contacts, terminals and parts do not exceed the temperature-rise limits of Table V (IEC 694 4.4.2), protecting against accelerated ageing of materials. Per [[iec-56]] 6.3 (with IEC 694 6.3), a breaker without series accessories is tested at its rated normal current; where series-connected accessories with a range of rated currents are fitted, additional tests are run at the rated current of each accessory (6.3.2). Temperatures and rises are measured per 6.3.3 and referred to ambient air temperature per 6.3.4, with auxiliary equipment covered in 6.3.5 and interpretation per 6.3.6 ([[iec-56]] 6.3). After a [[short-circuit-test]], contacts must still carry rated normal current within 10 K of these limits (6.102.8.2). Related: [[type-test]], [[short-circuit-test]].
mechanical-and-environmental-test: Mechanical and environmental tests prove that the circuit-breaker operates reliably over its rated supply-voltage, pressure and climatic range. Per [[iec-56]] 6.101, the core mechanical operation test (6.101.2) is 2000 no-load operating cycles per Table XII at minimum, rated and maximum control voltage/operating pressure, with no maintenance or adjustment allowed (lubrication excepted). Operating characteristics — closing/opening times, speeds, time spreads, recharging time, tightness, main-circuit resistance — are recorded before and after (6.101.1.2). Environmental tests, made by agreement, include low/high-temperature tests at T1 (minus 25 C or minus 40 C) and 40 C with 24 h soaks plus 50 close/50 open operations (6.101.3), a humidity test of 350 cycles between 25 C and 40 C above 95% RH (6.101.4), severe-ice operation (6.101.5) and static terminal-load tests for outdoor breakers at or above 52 kV (6.101.6). See [[type-test]], [[short-circuit-test]].
short-circuit-test: The short-circuit making and breaking tests prove the circuit-breaker can make and break all symmetrical and asymmetrical currents up to its [[rated-short-circuit-breaking-current]] at rated voltage. Per [[iec-56]] 6.102, this is deemed proved if the breaker makes and breaks the specified three-phase currents between 10% and 100% of rated, with single-phase duty at U/sqrt(3) also required for earthed-neutral or single-pole use. Tests may be direct or synthetic (6.102.4), and three-phase performance is preferably proved in three-phase circuits; single-pole, unit and multi-part testing (6.102.1, 6.102.3) are permitted within facility limits. Operation uses minimum operating voltage/pressure (6.102.2). After each [[test-duty]] the breaker must still carry and switch rated normal current (6.102.8). The detailed quantities, procedure and standardised duties are in [[short-circuit-test-quantities]], [[short-circuit-test-procedure]] and [[test-duty]] ([[iec-56]] 6.102-6.106).
short-circuit-test-quantities: Sub-clause 6.104 of [[iec-56]] fixes the electrical quantities for each [[short-circuit-test]]. Unless a tolerance is given, tests must be no less severe than the specified values. Applied voltage before making tests is U/sqrt(3) (phase-to-earth) for single-phase, averaging U/sqrt(3) for three-phase, not exceeding +10% (6.104.1). The short-circuit breaking current is stated as the average r.m.s. a.c. component in all phases plus the percentage maximum d.c. component, measured at contact separation per Figure 8, with the a.c. component not below 90% at final arc extinction (6.104.3-6.104.4). The prospective [[transient-recovery-voltage]] is specified by reference, delay and ITRV lines via two- or four-parameter envelopes, with standard values tabulated per duty and rated voltage (6.104.5, Tables II/XIV-XVII). Power-frequency recovery voltage equals U/sqrt(3) (or x first-pole-to-clear factor), held at least 0.1 s at 95% or more (6.104.7). See [[test-duty]], [[short-circuit-test-procedure]].
short-circuit-test-procedure: Sub-clause 6.105 of [[iec-56]] governs how the [[short-circuit-test]] series is executed. Time intervals between operations follow the [[rated-operating-sequence]] (4.104); the nominal 3 min interval may extend to 10 min for plant reasons (once per series longer) but not be shorter than 2 min, with actual intervals recorded (6.105.1). For breaking tests, auxiliary opening-release power is applied after short-circuit initiation where practicable, demonstrating the breaker is not pre-tripped (6.105.2); in make-break tests it is not applied until the breaker is closed and at least one half-cycle after contact make (6.105.3). Satisfactory latching on the [[rated-short-circuit-making-current]] must be proved, repeated at reduced voltage with negligible a.c. decrement if needed (6.105.4). Invalid parts of a duty cycle may be repeated without reconditioning (6.105.5). The duties themselves and their currents are defined in [[test-duty]] ([[iec-56]] 6.106).
test-duty: The basic short-circuit test series consists of five standardised Test-duties Nos. 1-5 per [[iec-56]] 6.106, each based on the [[rated-operating-sequence]] and expressed as percentages of the [[rated-short-circuit-breaking-current]]. Test-duty No. 1 is opening-only at 10% (d.c. below 20%); No. 2 at 30%; No. 3 at 60%; No. 4 the full rated operating sequence at 100% breaking and 100% making current with applied voltage per 6.104.1 (and may be split into making duty 4a and breaking duty 4b); No. 5 (applied only where the opening time t0 is below 80 ms) is opening-only at 100% breaking with the rated asymmetrical d.c. component. Each carries the prospective [[transient-recovery-voltage]] and power-frequency recovery voltage of 6.104.5 and 6.104.7. Breaking current may depart up to 20% (duties 1-2) or 10% (duty 3); peak making current up to 110% rated (duties 4, 4b, 5) ([[iec-56]] 6.106). See [[short-circuit-test-procedure]], [[short-circuit-test-quantities]].
making-and-breaking-capacity: Making and breaking capacity is the short-circuit performance the [[short-circuit-test]] verifies: the ability to make and break all symmetrical and asymmetrical currents up to the [[rated-short-circuit-breaking-current]] at rated voltage. Per [[iec-56]] 6.102.1, this is demonstrated by making and breaking the specified three-phase currents between 10% (or lower critical currents per 6.107) and 100% of rated at rated voltage, plus single-phase duty at U/sqrt(3) for earthed-neutral or single-pole application. Proof is provided through the standardised [[test-duty]] series of 6.106 under the quantities of [[short-circuit-test-quantities]]. After a duty the breaker must still make and break its rated normal current though its short-circuit capacity may be impaired (6.102.8.2) ([[iec-56]] 6.102).
